attempts.raw_response: Toss everything together until the pasta is evenly coated. If the sauce seems too thick, add a splash of the reserved pasta water to loosen it up. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper. Serve immediately, garnished with fresh herbs or grated cheese if desired.

Toss everything together until the pasta is evenly coated with the sauce. If the sauce seems too thick, add a splash of the reserved pasta water to loosen it up—this helps the sauce cling better to the noodles. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt, pepper, or a pinch of red pepper flakes for heat. Serve immediately, garnished with fresh parsley or grated Parmesan cheese if desired. This dish pairs well with a simple green salad and crusty bread for a complete meal.

Use tongs to toss the mixture. Serve with extra tomato sauce and Parmesan cheese.
Wash the mussels thoroughly with cold water. Beard them and scrub off any grit. Discard any mussels with open shells. Pour the cream, lemon, chicken stock, and salt and pepper into a deep cast iron skillet or another deep pan. Heat the ingredients over medium heat, bringing them to a light simmer. Place the mussels in the skillet, cover, and cook the mussels for about 5 minutes, or until their shells open. Remove the skillet from heat. Fill the pot about 3/4 full, and put in a few pinches of salt to add some flavor to the noodles. Break them up so all the noodles fit.
pair.prefix: If necessary, break them so all the noodles fit. This is the state at which the pasta is fully cooked, but still has a good texture, and hasn't become too mushy. It should take 5 - 10 minutes. Place a colander or strainer over the sink. Pour the pasta into the colander or strainer to drain the water. Transfer the pasta to a large bowl. Pour the sauce from the skillet into the bowl with the pasta.
